title: Radiopaque orbital foreign bodies from retained infant brachytherapy seeds

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:

【Purpose · abstract-1-1】The purpose of this case report is to describe a rare case of retained orbital brachytherapy seeds implanted during infancy and identified in an older adult undergoing neurocognitive evaluation. It highlights a multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management.

【Claim of priority · p0050】After conducting a literature review on September 16, 2026, utilizing PubMed and Google Scholar with the keywords “orbital brachytherapy, radon seeds, radon-222, retained orbital foreign body, eyelid radon seed, orbit radon seed extrusion”, we did not identify prior reports describing retained orbital radon-222 brachytherapy seeds implanted in infancy and surgically removed more than eight decades later to facilitate magnetic resonance imaging.

evidence.text: The purpose of this case report is to describe a rare case of retained orbital brachytherapy seeds implanted during infancy and identified in an older adult undergoing neurocognitive evaluation. It highlights a multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management.

After conducting a literature review on September 16, 2026, utilizing PubMed and Google Scholar with the keywords “orbital brachytherapy, radon seeds, radon-222, retained orbital foreign body, eyelid radon seed, orbit radon seed extrusion”, we did not identify prior reports describing retained orbital radon-222 brachytherapy seeds implanted in infancy and surgically removed more than eight decades later to facilitate magnetic resonance imaging.

【Patient consent · p0045】Written consent to publish this case has been obtained.

【Case presentation · p0010】An 85-year-old man with a prior history of resected cutaneous melanoma, proctectomy due to prostate cancer, primary open angle glaucoma, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment was referred to the oculoplastics service for evaluation of life-long radiopaque foreign bodies along the right periocular region. The foreign bodies were requested to be removed prior to proceeding with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for neurocognitive workup and evaluation by his neurologist. On further questioning, the patient reports a history of radiation therapy via “seed placement” to the right orbital region at 18 months of age in 1940 for a right superior orbital mass, while residing in Scotland. Childhood photographs reveal a right superior orbital mass (Fig. 1A), raising suspicion for a capillary hemangioma; however, the original medical records have become inaccessible.

The foreign bodies were requested to be removed prior to proceeding with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for neurocognitive workup and evaluation by his neurologist. On further questioning, the patient reports a history of radiation therapy via “seed placement” to the right orbital region at 18 months of age in 1940 for a right superior orbital mass, while residing in Scotland. Childhood photographs reveal a right superior orbital mass (Fig. 1A), raising suspicion for a capillary hemangioma; however, the original medical records have become inaccessible.

【Conclusions and importance · abstract-3-1】This case highlights the importance of recognizing historical radiation treatments as potential causes of orbital foreign bodies and imaging artifacts in older adult patients. It also underscores the value of multidisciplinary management for the safety of patients.

【Case presentation · p0015】The patient denied vision loss or ocular discomfort. Examination revealed stable best corrected visual acuity of 20/30 in both eyes with intraocular pressures of 14 mmHg in the right eye (OD) and 12 mmHg in the left eye (OS). Glaucoma medications administered in both eyes included travoprost 0.004% nightly and dorzolamide-timolol preservative-free 2%-0.5% twice daily. Dilated fundus examination was unremarkable bilaterally. Pre-operative computed tomography scan of the face revealed two discrete radiopaque foreign bodies. One, approximately 0.7 cm, was found in the superior right orbit below the orbital rim at the 11:00 position (Fig. 1B). A second, approximately 0.6 cm, was found within the right medial nasal soft tissue (Fig. 1C).

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 An 85-year-old man with retained radiopaque foreign bodies and a history of childhood orbital radiation using “seed placement.” (A) Childhood photograph demonstrating a right superior orbital mass before radiation treatment. Preoperative computed tomography demonstrating radiopaque foreign bodies (arrows) in the (B) superior right orbit and (C) right medial nasal region. (D) Postoperative radiography confirming complete removal of the foreign bodies.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Intraoperative removal of the presumed radon brachytherapy seeds from the right periocular (top) and nasal (bottom) region in an 85-year-old man with a history of childhood “seed placement” orbital radiation for presumed capillary hemangioma.
